Lecture 15 · Assessment · CO1

Twenty questions, thirty-five assignment problems, five projects

All items map to CO1. Bloom levels are suggested, not an official mapping. Solutions sit in collapsed boxes marked faculty.

20-question quiz10 descriptive · 15 numerical5 circuit design · 5 GRC/MATLAB tasks5 PBL projects + rubric

QuizTwenty questions (30 minutes)

1. A 4 kHz audio signal is to be radiated with a quarter-wave antenna. Roughly how long would the antenna be at baseband? U1 · L2 Understand · Easy

λ = c/f = 75 km, λ/4 = 18.75 km — the main reason we modulate onto a carrier.

2. Multiplying m(t) by cos(2πf_c t) produces a spectrum that is U1 · L2 Understand · Easy

Modulation property: m(t)cos ω_c t ↔ ½[M(f−f_c)+M(f+f_c)].

3. An AM envelope swings between 12 V and 4 V. The modulation index is U2 · L3 Apply · Easy

μ = (A_max − A_min)/(A_max + A_min) = 8/16 = 0.5.

4. A 1 kW carrier is amplitude modulated with μ = 0.8. The total transmitted power is U2 · L3 Apply · Medium

P_t = P_c(1 + μ²/2) = 1000(1 + 0.32) = 1.32 kW.

5. The maximum transmission efficiency of conventional AM without over-modulation is U2 · L2 Understand · Easy

η = μ²/(2+μ²) = 1/3 at μ = 1.

6. For a message of bandwidth W, the transmission bandwidth of SSB-SC is U3 · L1 Remember · Easy

Only one sideband is sent.

7. In a DSB-SC coherent detector the local carrier has a 60° phase error. The output amplitude, relative to perfect sync, is U3 · L4 Analyse · Medium

Output ∝ cos φ = cos 60° = 0.5 (verified in E2).

8. A diode-ring modulator fed with a message and a carrier ideally produces U4 · L2 Understand · Medium

The ring acts as a polarity switch: m(t)·sgn(cos ω_c t); the band-pass output is DSB-SC.

9. For μ = 0.6 and f_m = 2 kHz, the largest RC that avoids diagonal clipping is about U5 · L3 Apply · Medium

RC ≤ √(1−μ²)/(μω_m) = 0.8/(0.6·2π·2000) = 106.1 µs (E3).

10. The figure of merit of an SSB coherent receiver compared with a DSB-SC coherent receiver is U5 · L2 Understand · Medium

Both have figure of merit 1.

11. A superhet with f_IF = 455 kHz and LO above the signal is tuned to 700 kHz. The image frequency is U6 · L3 Apply · Easy

f_si = f_s + 2f_IF = 700 + 910 = 1610 kHz.

12. Image rejection in a superheterodyne receiver is provided by U6 · L4 Analyse · Hard

The image produces exactly f_IF at the mixer output, so only filtering before the mixer can remove it (E7, G6).

13. An FM signal has peak deviation 75 kHz for a 15 kHz tone. Its modulation index is U7 · L3 Apply · Easy

β = Δf/f_m = 5.

14. The Carson bandwidth of the FM signal in Q13 is U7 · L3 Apply · Easy

B_T = 2(Δf + f_m) = 2(90) = 180 kHz.

15. With f_m = 1 kHz, the carrier component of a tone-modulated FM signal first disappears when the deviation is U7 · L4 Analyse · Medium

J₀(β) = 0 first at β = 2.405 (E4, G3).

16. In an Armstrong transmitter, a mixer stage is used to U8 · L2 Understand · Medium

Mixing translates the carrier; only multiplication changes the deviation.

17. A limiter is placed before a Foster–Seeley discriminator to U9 · L2 Understand · Medium

The Foster–Seeley detector responds to amplitude as well as frequency.

18. A 75 µs de-emphasis network has its 3 dB corner at about U9 · L3 Apply · Medium

f₁ = 1/(2πτ) = 2122 Hz.

19. Above threshold, doubling the frequency deviation of an FM system (same W, same γ) changes the output SNR by about U9 · L4 Analyse · Hard

(SNR)_o ∝ D², so ×4 = +6 dB (at the cost of bandwidth).

20. A tone of fixed amplitude is applied to a phase modulator. As the tone frequency is doubled, the peak frequency deviation U10 · L4 Analyse · Hard

PM: Δf = k_p A_m f_m grows with f_m (E6, G5); in FM it would stay the same.

DescriptiveA1–A10

A1 · U1 · BTL L2 · Easy

Explain, with numbers, three reasons why a voice signal is modulated onto a carrier before radiation.

Solution faculty

Antenna size (λ/4 at 3 kHz = 25 km vs 75 m at 1 MHz); frequency-division multiplexing of many stations; matching the propagation band (ground/sky/LOS); narrowbanding; FM noise trade-off. Full marks need a numerical antenna example.

A2 · U4 · BTL L4 · Medium

Compare square-law, switching, balanced (diode-ring) and Gilbert-cell product modulators: principle, output, efficiency and where each is used.

Solution faculty

Square-law: a₂v² term, needs f_c > 3W, low efficiency, teaching. Switching: diode switched by large carrier, k_a = 4/(πA_c). Balanced/ring: carrier cancels → DSB-SC, 30–40 dB suppression in practice, mixers. Gilbert/AD633: four-quadrant multiplier, low-level AM or DSB-SC and synchronous detection.

A3 · U3 · BTL L4 · Medium

Derive the phase-shift (Hartley) SSB equation and compare the filter, phase-shift and Weaver methods.

Solution faculty

s = ½A_c[m cos ω_c t ∓ m̂ sin ω_c t]; sign gives USB/LSB. Filter: sharp crystal filter, needs gap near DC. Phase-shift: wideband 90° shifter, balance critical. Weaver: two quadrature stages, avoids wideband Hilbert, used in DSP/SDR.

A4 · U5 · BTL L4 · Medium

Derive the condition for avoiding diagonal clipping in an envelope detector and explain negative-peak clipping. Sketch both distortions.

Solution faculty

RC ≤ √(1−μ²)/(μω_m) from requiring the exponential decay slope to exceed the envelope slope (max at cos ω_m t = −μ). Negative-peak clipping when R_ac/R_dc < μ; troughs flattened.

A5 · U6 · BTL L5 · Medium

Explain the superheterodyne principle. Justify the choice of 455 kHz IF for MW AM and 10.7 MHz for FM in terms of image rejection and selectivity.

Solution faculty

Fixed IF gives constant selectivity and gain. Higher IF → image further away (better image rejection) but harder to get narrow bandwidth; lower IF → better adjacent-channel selectivity, worse image. 455 kHz: 910 kHz image offset vs 9–10 kHz channels. 10.7 MHz: image 21.4 MHz away, outside the 20 MHz FM band; 200 kHz channel bandwidth easy at 10.7 MHz.

A6 · U7 · BTL L2 · Easy

Distinguish narrowband and wideband FM. Show why NBFM has the same bandwidth as AM but is not the same signal.

Solution faculty

NBFM β ≪ 1: s ≈ A_c cos ω_c t − βA_c sin ω_m t sin ω_c t; sidebands in quadrature with the carrier (phasor rotates, amplitude nearly constant) vs AM in phase (amplitude varies). Both B_T ≈ 2f_m. WBFM β ≳ 1, many Bessel sidebands, Carson.

A7 · U8 · BTL L4 · Medium

Compare direct (VCO/varactor) and indirect (Armstrong) FM generation. Why does the Armstrong method need frequency multipliers and a mixer?

Solution faculty

Direct: large Δf, needs AFC/PLL for stability, varactor non-linearity. Indirect: crystal stable, NBFM with small Δf₁ (linear), multipliers raise Δf and f_c together, mixer brings f_c to the right value without changing Δf.

A8 · U9 · BTL L5 · Medium

Compare slope, Foster–Seeley, ratio, quadrature and PLL FM detectors in linearity, AM rejection and complexity. Which would you choose for an IC receiver and why?

Solution faculty

Slope: poor linearity, no AM rejection. Foster–Seeley: linear, needs limiter. Ratio: built-in AM rejection, half output. Quadrature: one coil, IF ICs. PLL: best threshold, integrable, no coils → IC choice (or quadrature).

A9 · U9 · BTL L4 · Hard

Explain pre-emphasis/de-emphasis, the FM threshold effect and the capture effect. Why do aviation radios still use AM?

Solution faculty

Parabolic noise PSD → boost high frequencies before, cut after: 10–13 dB gain. Threshold: below CNR ≈ 10 dB clicks, SNR collapses. Capture: stronger FM signal suppresses weaker. Aviation AM: two simultaneous transmissions are both heard (no capture), safety; narrow channels; simple.

A10 · U10, U11 · BTL L4 · Hard

Show how FM can be generated with a phase modulator and PM with a frequency modulator. Draw the PLL and explain how it demodulates FM. Explain the FM stereo multiplex as an application of the whole module.

Solution faculty

Integrate m then PM → FM; differentiate then FM → PM. PLL: PD → LF → VCO; in lock v(t) = k_f m(t)/k_v. Stereo MPX: L+R 0–15 kHz, pilot 19 kHz, L−R DSB-SC at 38 kHz, RDS 57 kHz, all frequency-modulating the carrier.

NumericalN1–N15

N1 · U2 · BTL L3 · Easy

A carrier of 20 V peak across 50 Ω is amplitude modulated with μ = 0.6. Find the carrier power, total sideband power, total power and efficiency.

Solution faculty

P_c = 20²/(2·50) = 4 W. P_SB = P_c μ²/2 = 4·0.18 = 0.72 W. P_t = 4.72 W. η = 0.72/4.72 = 15.25 %.

N2 · U2 · BTL L3 · Easy

An AM envelope has A_max = 150 V and A_min = 50 V. Find μ and the unmodulated carrier amplitude.

Solution faculty

μ = (150−50)/(150+50) = 0.5. A_c = (A_max + A_min)/2 = 100 V.

N3 · U2 · BTL L3 · Easy

The antenna current of an AM transmitter is 10 A unmodulated. Find the current when μ = 0.8.

Solution faculty

I_t = I_c√(1 + μ²/2) = 10√1.32 = 11.49 A.

N4 · U2 · BTL L3 · Medium

A 10 kW carrier is modulated simultaneously by two tones with μ₁ = 0.6 and μ₂ = 0.4. Find the effective index and the total power.

Solution faculty

μ_t = √(0.36 + 0.16) = 0.721. P_t = 10(1 + 0.52/2) = 12.6 kW.

N5 · U3 · BTL L3 · Easy

For μ = 1, find the percentage power saved by transmitting DSB-SC and SSB instead of AM, for the same sideband power.

Solution faculty

P_t = 1.5P_c; DSB-SC sends 0.5P_c → saving 66.7 %; SSB sends 0.25P_c → saving 83.3 %.

N6 · U5 · BTL L3 · Medium

An envelope detector receives AM with μ = 0.7 and f_m = 5 kHz. Find the maximum RC for no diagonal clipping.

Solution faculty

RC_max = √(1−0.49)/(0.7·2π·5000) = 0.714/21991 = 32.47 µs.

N7 · U6 · BTL L3 · Medium

A superhet with f_IF = 455 kHz (LO above) is tuned to 1000 kHz. Its pre-selector has Q = 100. Find the image frequency, ρ and the image rejection in dB.

Solution faculty

f_si = 1910 kHz; ρ = 1.91 − 0.5236 = 1.3864; α = √(1 + (100·1.3864)²) = 138.6 → 42.8 dB.

N8 · U6 · BTL L4 · Hard

An MW receiver covers 540–1650 kHz with f_IF = 455 kHz. Find the LO frequency ratio and capacitance ratio for the LO above the signal, and the capacitance ratio for the RF stage. Why is the LO not placed below?

Solution faculty

LO 995–2105 kHz: ratio 2.116, C ratio 4.48. RF: 1650/540 = 3.056, C ratio 9.34. LO below: 85–1195 kHz, ratio 14.06, C ratio ≈ 198 — impractical.

N9 · U7 · BTL L3 · Easy

A 3 kHz tone of 5 V peak frequency-modulates a carrier with k_f = 15 kHz/V. Find Δf, β and the Carson bandwidth.

Solution faculty

Δf = 75 kHz; β = 25; B_T = 2(75 + 3) = 156 kHz.

N10 · U7 · BTL L4 · Medium

An FM signal with A_c = 10 V across 50 Ω has β = 2 and f_m = 5 kHz. Find the power in the carrier, the first and second sideband pairs, the fraction within n ≤ 3 and the Carson bandwidth. (J₀ = 0.2239, J₁ = 0.5767, J₂ = 0.3528, J₃ = 0.1289.)

Solution faculty

P = 1 W. Carrier 0.0501 W; first pair 2·0.5767² = 0.665 W; second pair 0.249 W; third pair 0.033 W; n ≤ 3: 99.76 %. B_T = 2(10 + 5) = 30 kHz.

N11 · U8 · BTL L4 · Hard

An Armstrong transmitter starts at f₁ = 200 kHz with Δf₁ = 25 Hz. It uses a ×64 multiplier, a mixer with a 10.9 MHz crystal oscillator (difference taken) and a ×48 multiplier. Find the carrier and deviation at each point.

Solution faculty

×64: 12.8 MHz, 1.6 kHz. Mixer: 12.8 − 10.9 = 1.9 MHz, 1.6 kHz. ×48: 91.2 MHz, 76.8 kHz.

N12 · U7 · BTL L3 · Easy

s(t) = 10 cos[2π·10⁷t + 5 sin(4000πt)]. Find β, Δf and the Carson bandwidth.

Solution faculty

f_m = 2 kHz; β = 5; Δf = 10 kHz; B_T = 24 kHz.

N13 · U10 · BTL L3 · Medium

A first-order PLL has K_d = 0.25 V/rad and K_o = 2π × 40 kHz/V. The input is 5 kHz from the free-running VCO frequency. Find the loop gain, the steady-state phase error (sinusoidal PD) and the hold-in range.

Solution faculty

K = 0.25 · 2π · 40 000 = 62 832 s⁻¹ (10 kHz). sin θ_e = 5/10 → θ_e = 30°. Hold-in ±10 kHz.

N14 · U9 · BTL L3 · Easy

A de-emphasis network uses R = 7.5 kΩ and C = 10 nF. Find f₁ and the SNR improvement for W = 15 kHz.

Solution faculty

τ = 75 µs; f₁ = 2122 Hz; W/f₁ = 7.07; I = 7.07³/(3(7.07 − tan⁻¹7.07)) = 20.9 → 13.2 dB.

N15 · U5, U9 · BTL L4 · Hard

A broadcast FM system (Δf = 75 kHz, W = 15 kHz) and an AM system (μ = 1, envelope detection) both have γ = 30 dB. Find each output SNR (no emphasis) and the FM carrier-to-noise ratio in the Carson bandwidth. Is the FM receiver above threshold?

Solution faculty

FM: 1.5·25 = 37.5 → 30 + 15.7 = 45.7 dB. AM: γ/3 → 25.2 dB. CNR = γ·W/B_T = 30 − 10log(180/15) = 19.2 dB > ≈10 dB → above threshold.

Circuit designD1–D5

D1 · U6 · BTL L6 · Medium

Design a 455 kHz IF tank with L = 150 µH and a 10 kHz bandwidth. Find C (choose a standard value), the required loaded Q and the parallel resistance R_p.

Solution faculty

C = 1/((2π·455k)²·150µ) = 815.7 pF → 820 pF. Q = 455/10 = 45.5. R_p = Qω₀L = 45.5·428.8 = 19.5 kΩ. Verify by adapting C02 netlist.

D2 · U5 · BTL L6 · Medium

Design a diode envelope detector for f_c = 455 kHz, f_m(max) = 4.5 kHz, μ = 0.8, feeding a 47 kΩ amplifier input through a coupling capacitor.

Solution faculty

RC_max = 0.6/(0.8·2π·4500) = 26.5 µs; RC ≫ 2.2 µs. Choose 4.7 kΩ and 4.7 nF (22.1 µs). R_ac/R_dc = (4.7k∥47k)/4.7k = 0.909 ≥ 0.8 ✓. Coupling capacitor 1 µF.

D3 · U6, U8 · BTL L6 · Medium

Design a 10.7 MHz Colpitts oscillator with L = 1 µH and C₁ = C₂. Find the required series capacitance and the frequency obtained with standard 470 pF capacitors.

Solution faculty

C_eq = 1/((2π·10.7M)²·1µ) = 221 pF → C₁ = C₂ = 442 pF. With 470 pF: C_eq = 235 pF → 10.38 MHz. Trim with a small parallel capacitor or adjust L. Start from C04.

D4 · U9 · BTL L6 · Easy

Design a 50 µs de-emphasis network with C = 2.2 nF. Choose a standard resistor and find the resulting corner frequency.

Solution faculty

R = 50µ/2.2n = 22.7 kΩ → 22 kΩ; τ = 48.4 µs; f₁ = 3288 Hz (theory 3183 Hz). Verify with C01.

D5 · U8 · BTL L6 · Hard

A varactor VCO uses L = 2.2 µH at 10.7 MHz. Find the total tank capacitance and the capacitance change for Δf = 75 kHz.

Solution faculty

C = 1/((2π·10.7M)²·2.2µ) = 100.6 pF. ΔC ≈ 2CΔf/f = 2·100.6·75k/10.7M = 1.41 pF. Use C07 to check the tuning range.

Lab tasksT1–T5 (GNU Radio, MATLAB, Python)

T1 · U12 · BTL L3 · Easy

G7 RTL-SDR: receive three local FM stations. For each record frequency, gain, peak level and measured occupied bandwidth, and compare with Carson's rule (Δf = 75 kHz, W = 15 kHz).

Solution faculty

Occupied bandwidth ≈ 150–200 kHz; Carson 180 kHz. Results depend on local stations; check consistency and screenshots.

T2 · U2, U5 · BTL L4 · Medium

G1/E1/E3: set μ = 0.5, 1.0, 1.3. Capture the envelope and coherent outputs; explain the differences. Then set φ = 0, 45, 90° and tabulate the coherent output amplitude.

Solution faculty

Envelope output distorts for μ > 1; coherent output stays sinusoidal. Coherent amplitude ∝ cos φ: 1, 0.707, 0.

T3 · U7 · BTL L4 · Medium

E4/G3: find the deviation values (f_m = 1 kHz) at which the carrier and the first sideband vanish; compare with the zeros of J₀ and J₁.

Solution faculty

Carrier nulls at Δf = 2.405, 5.520, 8.654 kHz; J₁ nulls at 3.832, 7.016 kHz.

T4 · U6 · BTL L5 · Medium

E7/G6: plot the desired-to-image ratio against pre-selector Q (5–100) and overlay the theoretical IFRR. Explain any difference.

Solution faculty

Measured follows α = √(1 + Q²ρ²); E7 values 29.9 dB (Q 20) and 39.4 dB (Q 60) are about 1 dB above theory because the IF filter adds a little extra discrimination.

T5 · U9, U10 · BTL L5 · Hard

E8/G4: vary the PLL natural frequency (0.5, 1, 2, 4 kHz) and loop bandwidth. Measure settling time and demodulated SNR; explain the trade-off.

Solution faculty

Wider loop → faster settling (≈ 4/(ζω_n)), tracks larger f_m, but more noise passes → lower SNR; too narrow → cannot follow the message (distortion). E8: f_n = 2 kHz gives 0.37 ms settling and gain 0.303.

PBLFive three-week projects

Week 1 analysis and design · week 2 simulation in two tools · week 3 demo, 6-page IEEE report, 10-minute talk.

PBL-1 · Campus AM announcement link

1 MHz carrier; choose μ and compute P_t and η for 100 mW; Colpitts carrier (C04) and diode-ring or AD633 modulator; envelope detector and 455 kHz IF stage; simulate in G1 with noise. Hardware only into a 50 Ω dummy load or by cable.

PBL-2 · FM wireless microphone (design study)

Varactor VCO for Δf = 75 kHz with a 100 mV audio peak (note the k_v this needs vs C07's 10 kHz/V); 50 µs pre-emphasis; PLL receiver (E8); full chain in GNU Radio. No over-the-air transmission.

PBL-3 · SDR FM broadcast monitor

Extend G7 to scan 88–108 MHz in 200 kHz steps and log levels; measure occupied bandwidth of three stations vs Carson; show the 19 kHz pilot, L−R at 38 kHz and RDS at 57 kHz. Receive only.

PBL-4 · AM vs FM vs PM over one channel ★ (integrated)

Same message (W = 3.4 kHz), same received power, same white noise, 30 kHz bandwidth limit. Plot SNR_o against γ for AM (envelope and coherent), DSB-SC, SSB, FM and PM; mark the FM threshold; add a co-channel interferer to show capture; recommend a scheme for party-line voice, music and minimum bandwidth.

PBL-5 · Superheterodyne MW front end

531–1602 kHz, IF 455 kHz, ≥ 40 dB image rejection at the top of the band: find ρ, the pre-selector Q (one or two stages), the IF tank (C02/C03) and LO tracking; verify in E7 and G6.

RequisitesBefore and after this module

Pre-requisites

  • Fourier transform, modulation property, LTI filters, Hilbert transform
  • Product-to-sum trigonometric identities
  • Diode and BJT biasing, RLC resonance and Q, op-amps
  • Random variables, PSD, white noise N₀/2
  • Basic Python or MATLAB; GNU Radio Companion installed

Post-requisites

  • Digital modulation: ASK, PSK, FSK, QAM reuse the coherent receiver and Costas loop
  • Wireless and mobile systems: superhet and direct-conversion front ends, PLL synthesisers
  • Software-defined radio: G7 is the template for later SDR labs
  • RF circuit design: tuned amplifiers, oscillators, mixers, detectors
